WHAT THE CENSUS ESTABLISHED, and it re-frames this function: regnorm reports 98 STRUCTURAL rows, but 93 are branch-displacement artifacts of the single missing instruction, and of the 5 GENUINE rows FOUR ARE BENIGN RELOCATION-NAMING ARTIFACTS - `@0x58/@0x5c` and `@0x4e4/@0x4e8`, where the target cites `jumptable_8011CAD4` / `jumptable_8011CA9C` and ours cites `@2725` / `@2727`. Both sides emit their own compiler-generated switch jump table; the DOL splitter invented the `jumptable_` names for the extracted ones exactly as it invents `lbl_` names for pool constants. This is the SAME benign artifact class documented for fn_8005FDA8's .sdata2 constants in attempt.GW_fn8005fda8-pool-label-artifact-not-a-wrong-symbol-defect.20260901.v1, now shown to extend to JUMP TABLES. It is not source-reachable and must not be 'fixed'.

SO THE ENTIRE LIVE RESIDUAL IS ONE INSTRUCTION, fully characterised: at +0xa8 the target emits `lwz r0,224(r28)` / `cmpwi r0,25` / `mr r29,r0` / `blt ->0xc8`; ours emits `lwz r29,224(r28)` / `cmpwi r29,25` / `blt ->0xc4`. Same destination register r29 on both sides, so this is NOT a colouring or numbering choice - it is purely whether MWCC loads through a scratch temp and homes it, or loads straight into the callee-saved register. Source shape is `s32 amount = *(s32*)&item->data[4]; if (amount >= 25) { msgPost(...); } PlayerGiveGold(player->index, amount);` and it is already the read-once form that attempt.fn-8005d730-read-once-unpark.20260831.v1 correctly installed.
